The '''KYD-21''' was a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] favored by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] during the decades leading up to the establishment of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Description==
This compact [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] was crafted from [[Hadrium alloy/Legends|hadrium]] alloy, and featured a ridged handgrip with guardless trigger. The muzzle featured a brake to absorb the emitter flash, and both the igniter pin and blaster gas loading port were located on the grip beneath the [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]]. The pistol was noted for its impressive stopping power, despite its small size, and, though expensive, became popular amongst assassins for its subtlety.

==History==
[[File:Grantagun.jpg|thumb|[[Granta Omega]]'s KYD-21 blaster pistol.]]
[[Granta Omega]] used this pistol to kill [[Darra Thel-Tanis]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="The Final Showdown">''[[Jedi Quest: The Final Showdown]]''</ref>

[[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] wielded a KYD-21 as her primary weapon, sometimes used in conjunction with a [[KiSteer 1284 projectile rifle/Legends|projectile rifle]] which fellow bounty hunter [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] insisted she use. The [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] [[Darman Skirata]] wielded a KYD-21 during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and [[Ghez Hokan]] was known to carry a custom version.

{{Weapon-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
In the scenes where Zam Wesell is talking to [[Jango Fett]] and when she loads the [[kouhun]]s in the droid [[ASN-121]] from [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] Zam can be seen sporting a [[WESTAR-34 blaster pistol]] in her holster instead of the usual KYD-21 she uses in later scenes and keeps in the same holster.<ref name="Episode II">{{Film|II}}</ref> The first two scenes&mdash;with the WESTAR&mdash;were done during [[Wikipedia:Pick-up (filmmaking)|pick-ups]] shooting in [[March]] [[2001]] in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]], while the others scenes were from [[Wikipedia:Principal photography|principal photography]] in [[July]] [[2000]] in [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australia]]. [[Pablo Hidalgo]] hypothesized that the [[Wikipedia:Prop|prop]] of the KDY might have not been sent to the United Kingdom for the pick-ups.<ref name="Blusky">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3mmkkoqklf22k|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2026-05-24|archivedate=20260524161354}}</ref>
